events.description: 28. ORDER TO SHOW CAUSE: In denying Plaintiffs' motion for preliminary injunction, the Court noted that Plaintiffs are unlikely to establish that they have standing to bring this suit due to a lack of Article III injury in fact and redressability. ECF No. 23. "[W]henever standing is unclear, [the Court] must consider it sua sponte to ensure there is an Article III case or controversy before [it]." Hobby Lobby Stores, Inc. v. Sebelius, 723 F.3d 1114, 1126 (10th Cir. 2013). The parties are therefore ordered to show cause why this case should not be dismissed for lack of Article III standing. Because Plaintiffs "bear the burden of establishing standing," Murthy v. Missouri, 144 S. Ct. 1972, 1986 (2024), Plaintiffs are directed to file a brief asserting grounds for standing with 14 days of this Order, Defendants shall then file a Response within 14 days of Plaintiffs' brief, and Plaintiffs may offer a Reply, if desired, within 7 days of Defendants' Response. Signed by District Judge Ann Marie McIff Allen on 4/1/25. (mkn) (Entered: 04/01/2025)
